candidates.change_summary: Change the update of pastBlockTime to use block.timestamp instead of block.timestamp + 1, allowing a call in the next block to succeed.
Delete the statement that updates pastBlockTime, so the variable never changes and the timestamp guard behaves differently on subsequent calls.
Change the guard from strict inequality to >= so calls in the immediately following block (timestamp equal to pastBlockTime) are allowed.
Change the payment check from == 10 ether to == 9 ether so calls with 9 ether now succeed and calls with 10 ether revert.
Change the timestamp guard from > pastBlockTime to >= pastBlockTime so a call in the same timestamp slot is no longer blocked.
Store block.timestamp without the +1 so consecutive timestamps are no longer allowed, blocking calls in the next block.
Change the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 != 0 so payouts happen on different blocks.
Delete the pastBlockTime update so the contract never records the call time, allowing multiple calls in the same timestamp slot.
Remove the assignment `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so pastBlockTime is never updated after a call.
Change the assignment to `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` instead of `block.timestamp + 1`.
Remove the `require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime);` check so multiple calls in the same block are allowed.
Change the payout condition from `block.number % 15 == 0` to `block.number % 15 != 0`.
Delete the statement updating pastBlockTime so it never advances.
Replace pastBlockTime update with block.timestamp instead of block.timestamp + 1.
Change the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 == 1.
Delete the payout transfer so the contract never sends funds back.
Replace the transfer amount with 1 ether instead of the whole contract balance.
